FLASHSCORE PREVIEW

Beşiktaş have a great opportunity to maintain their top-eight spot in the UEFA Europa League (UEL) when they take on Hapoel Be’er Sheva, whose campaign is seemingly close to being on its last legs, in Batumi, Georgia. 

Match News and Current Form

Beşiktaş are eighth in the UEL table despite failing to win their last two matches - the latest of which was a 3-2 defeat to Celtic - part of a poor run of form in which they won only one of five competitive encounters (D2, L2). Back-to-back Süper Lig victories since then though have been ideal preparation for this fixture in Batumi, which is hosting for security reasons. The Turkish giants come into this game off the back of a four-goal haul at the weekend and will likely be relying heavily again on their attack to compensate for a defensive unit that has kept just one clean sheet in their last 31 UEL main draw matches.

Be’er Sheva will play their first game in more than two weeks as they attempt to keep their slim hopes of progression alive. Now three points off the top 24 and with just one point (D1, L3), they are quickly running out of opportunities to progress beyond the main phase of a continental competition for the first time in four attempts since the 2016/17 season, after losing 2-0 to OFI Crete. It may be in their best interests to exit this competition soon anyway after their domestic league ambitions took a hit earlier this month with a 1-0 loss to Hapoel Tel Aviv, while their UEL main draw away form remains poor, with nine defeats in their last 11 such matches (D2). 

Head-to-Head History

Beşiktaş won both previous H2Hs, with those games being played in the 2016/17 UEL. 

Hot Stats and Streaks

Twelve of Beşiktaş’ last 14 matches produced over 2.5 goals.

Five of Beşiktaş’ last seven wins came by a 2+ goal margin.

Seven of the nine goals in Be’er Sheva’s league phase games this term arrived in the second half.

Be’er Sheva scored in nine of their last 12 European defeats. 

Key Players to Watch and Missing Players

Junior Olaitan has scored or assisted in all four of his UEL main draw appearances for Beşiktaş and could become just the second African player since 2009/10 to do so in his first five such UEL matches. Amankwah Forson remains Be’er Sheva’s only scorer in this league phase campaign, with six of his last seven goals for any club coming after half-time and six of the seven arriving in wins.

Beşiktaş’ Ümit Akdağ remains suspended, while Be’er Sheva have been without Eliel Peretz since late October due to injury.  

For all the latest team news, please check the Flashscore match centre.

Betting Analysis

Given that they have earned some handsome victories recently, backing Beşiktaş to win by 2+ goals seems sensible here.

Author: Aaron Murphy

FLASHSCORE PREVIEW

A faltering Celta Vigo look to break into the top 24 of the UEFA Europa League (UEL) against a rampant Bournemouth side who fly high in the league phase on the back of an unprecedented run of form. 

Match News and Current Form

After falling to a fourth straight winless La Liga game on Saturday (D2, L2), Celta Vigo look a long way from the side that have posted consecutive top-seven finishes. Reaching at least the quarter-final in their last two UEL appearances, the Sky Blues need to rally in the second half of this league phase after losing three of their opening four matches (W1). Celta’s five defeats in their last six UEL matches (W1) are just one fewer than they suffered in their first 26 games in the competition (W13, D7, L6), and playing at home isn’t a huge boost either, as Claudio Giráldez’s men have won just twice at Balaídos all season (D3, L4). 

Unlike their flailing hosts, Bournemouth secured a club-record ninth consecutive victory at the weekend, beating Nottingham Forest 2-0 to strengthen their European qualification bid. Yet another record beckons for the Cherries here as they could become the first English side to win their first five games in major European competition, one which would strengthen their claim to top the league phase table. Hitting the road shouldn’t faze Marco Rose’s men either as they have triumphed in both of their UEL trips despite failing to keep a clean sheet, including a 2-1 win on Spanish shores against Real Sociedad. 

Head-to-Head History

This is the first meeting between the sides and Celta’s first clash against any English team since 2016/17, though they’re winless in five against such opponents (D1, L4).

Hot Stats and Streaks

Five of the six UEL goals Celta have conceded this term came after half-time. 

Celta are the only side to lose more than one game after scoring first in the UEL this term (L2).

All seven of Bournemouth’s away matches this season produced over 2.5 goals.

Bournemouth’s last ten games featured over 7.5 corners.

Key Players to Watch and Missing Players

Pablo Durán is Celta’s joint-top scorer this season (G4), although his two goals in his last four appearances were both match openers in 2-1 defeats. Rayan has scored three goals from his opening four UEL appearances for Bournemouth, with only one Brazilian bettering that tally in this competition before they turned 21.

FLASHSCORE PREVIEW

Two sides well within the fight to directly qualify for the last 16 of the UEFA Europa League (UEL) battle it out in Croatia on matchday five as Dinamo Zagreb host Bayer Leverkusen.

Match News and Current Form

With seven points after four matches, Dinamo Zagreb remain on course to qualify for the knockout stages of this competition for a second successive campaign. The Blues begin this matchday sat just outside the top eight, with their defensive performances seeing them keep three clean sheets and underpinning their success thus far. That’s the same number of shutouts they managed across their prior 24 European fixtures, something the Croatian champions hope to replicate here as they look to win three of their first five group/league phase matches in a European campaign for the first time since 2020/21.

Bayer Leverkusen are also looking to take another step closer to the last 16, and are chasing a response to matchday four’s defeat to Marseille (1-0) which left them three points off the summit. Die Werkself boast the competition's joint-best defensive record having kept three clean sheets prior to that defeat, and a 4-0 rout of Paderborn in the Bundesliga on Saturday ought to have boosted confidence yet further. Four wins in their last five away matches reinforces Leverkusen’s tag as favourites here, as does an eight-game unbeaten run on the road in this competition (W6, D2) which has seen them keep five clean sheets.   

Head-to-Head History

This will be the first meeting between these sides, though Dinamo have lost their last eight European games against German teams.

Hot Stats and Streaks

Six of Dinamo’s last seven major European home matches saw a side score 3+ goals.

Only three teams have picked up fewer UEL yellow cards this season than Dinamo (5).

Six of Leverkusen’s eight UEL goals this term came before half-time.

Leverkusen have registered a joint-high 36 shots on target in this season’s UEL.

Key Players to Watch and Missing Players

Dinamo's Dion Beljo has scored more UEL goals than any other player (9) in the last two seasons, eight of which came on home soil. Leverkusen’s Aleix García has four goal contributions across his last five club games (G1, A3), with each of his last three strikes serving as match openers inside ten minutes.

Dinamo appear to be at full strength for this clash, though Leverkusen remain without Martin Terrier due to injury. 

For all the latest team news, please check the Flashscore match centre. 

Betting Analysis

With Dinamo performing well defensively and Leverkusen losing their last UEL outing, the draw market looks an enticing proposition here.

FLASHSCORE PREVIEW

Marseille are desperate for points in their quest to play knockout football in the UEFA Europa League (UEL), and now tackle a Levski Sofia side who are well placed in the league phase.

Match News and Current Form

Marseille’s four-match winning streak came to an abrupt halt on Sunday night as they let slip a two-goal lead in a remarkable 3-2 defeat to Le Mans. That result will be a worry for manager Bruno Génésio, whose side have now lost four of their last six outings on home soil (W2), with one of those reversals coming at home to Olympiacos in this competition and leaving the French outfit at risk of losing three major continental matches in a row at Stade Vélodrome for the first time since November 2020. They did at least beat Bayer Leverkusen 1-0 in their last UEL outing, but after tasting defeat in their opening three league phase fixtures, they’re already playing catch-up in the race for a top-24 finish.

Having seen a seven-match unbeaten run (W5, D2) come to an abrupt end before the international break, Levski Sofia bounced back to form emphatically by hammering Lokomotiv Sofia 4-1 on Sunday. That result leaves the Blues in second place in the Bulgarian top flight, and things are going pretty well in the UEL too, where two wins from four attempts (D1, L1) leave them well placed to reach the knockout stages of a continental competition for the first time since the 2005/06 UEFA Cup. One of those triumphs was a 2-1 victory at Plzeň earlier this month and means the Blues could now register three European successes on the spin for the first time across the same campaign since 1969.

Head-to-Head History

The only previous meeting between these two teams ended in a 1-0 victory for Levski in the 2005/06 UEFA Cup.

Hot Stats and Streaks

Marseille’s last 12 competitive matches saw both teams receive a yellow card.

Marseille’s last three UEL matches featured exactly one goal.

Only one team has had fewer shots on target than Levski Sofia (10) ahead of this round.

Levski’s four league phase games didn’t produce a single goal in the first 30 minutes.

Key Players to Watch and Missing Players

No player enters this round having had more shots off target than Marseille’s Igor Paixão (seven), but he could break that streak here with five of his last six club goals coming at home. Eight of Juan Perea’s last ten goals have come after half-time, while each of his five goalscoring appearances for Levski this season ended in victory.

Marseille hope to have Pierre-Emile Højbjerg available after illness, while Levski Sofia have no obvious fresh injury worries.

FLASHSCORE PREVIEW

Olympiacos will be looking to maintain their unbeaten record in the UEFA Europa League (UEL) this season as they face an AC Milan side at the wrong end of the table. 

Match News and Current Form

Olympiacos’ strong recent UEL form has continued this season (W3, D1), with the Greek giants now unbeaten in their last 11 such league phase games (W7, D4), conceding just twice in the process. They are also unbeaten in their last 12 competitive matches (W10, D2) under current manager Imanol Alguacil, with their latest outing seeing them thump Iraklis 6-2 on Sunday in domestic action. Their last UEL game against Rennes (0-0) did see the Red-Whites’ 100% main-draw record this term come to an end though, so they will be happy to be returning to the Karaiskakis Stadium, where they have won their last four home matches in the competition. 

Milan also shone at the weekend, thrashing Frosinone 5-1, but unlike Olympiacos, they have struggled in the UEL so far this season, losing three of their four such games (W1). They therefore find themselves 28th in the table, with the Rossoneri now under pressure to avoid suffering three successive defeats in major European competition without scoring for the first time ever, following 3-0 and 2-0 losses to Bournemouth and Ferencváros respectively. That result against the Cherries is Milan’s only competitive away defeat to date under Ruben Amorim though (W4, D3), raising hopes among supporters that their team can get something here. 

Head-to-Head History

Olympiacos have only won one of the previous four H2Hs (D1, L2), but that victory came in their most recent meeting with Milan in the UEL in December 2018 (3-1). 

Hot Stats and Streaks

Olympiacos’ last seven European games were decided by a one-goal margin at most. 

None of Olympiacos’ last 14 UEL matches featured over 3.5 goals. 

Milan haven't drawn any of their last nine games (W6, L3). 

Milan scored exactly two goals before the half-hour mark in four of their last five matches. 

Key Players to Watch and Missing Players

Jota Silva has had the most shots of any player in this season’s UEL main draw, but hasn't scored with any of those attempts, getting just two on target. Alphadjo Cisse is enjoying a superb breakthrough campaign with Milan, with the 20-year-old’s strike against Frosinone meaning that his last seven goals have all come before the hour mark, a run which includes his hat-trick against Salzburg (4-0) in the team’s only UEL win so far this term. 

After scoring twice at the weekend, Olympiacos’ Leon Bailey then went off injured, while Milan seemingly have no fresh absentees. 

For all the latest team news, please check the Flashscore match centre.

Betting Analysis

Given Olympiacos’ strong home form, backing the hosts to win combined with under 3.5 goals is tempting here. 

Author: Alex Bowmer

FLASHSCORE PREVIEW

Benfica look to maintain their perfect start to their UEFA Europa League (UEL) campaign as they head to Viktoria Plzeň, who are trying to build on their first league phase victory of the season.

Match News and Current Form

Plzeň started the league phase with three straight defeats before beating Lillestrøm 1-0 on matchday four to revitalise their qualification ambitions. Although Radoslav Kováč’s side are unbeaten across their last five competitive fixtures (W4, D1), their struggles at the Doosan Arena do not bode well as they’ve won just one of their last seven home games in all competitions (D2, L4). That includes both league phase fixtures here this term, while winning none of their last six UEL home matches (D4, L2) represents their longest such sequence in major European competition.

Benfica arrive in the Czech Republic hoping to put Plzeň under more pressure, as they sit on top of the league phase standings with a perfect record (W4) having spent 87% of their campaign in the lead - a comfortably higher ratio than any other side. That dominance has become second nature for Marco Silva’s side, who’ve won each of their last nine matches as they try to keep pace with Portuguese top-flight leaders Porto. The Eagles can also take plenty of encouragement from only losing two of their last nine away UEL proper games (W4, D3).

Head-to-Head History

This is the first meeting between these two clubs. Plzeň have lost just one of their previous five UEL meetings with Portuguese sides (W2, D2), while Benfica are facing Czech opposition for the first time since March 1992.

Hot Stats and Streaks

Plzeň conceded first in four of their six UEL games this term, including three of their four league phase fixtures.

Nine of Plzeň’s 11 home fixtures this term saw both teams score.

Benfica led at half-time in five of their last six European fixtures.

Benfica have scored at least twice in each of their last four away games.

Key Players to Watch and Missing Players

Prince Adu has scored twice across his last three Plzeň appearances, including the winner against Lillestrøm, with each of his last five goals in Europe arriving before half-time. Benfica’s Gianluca Prestianni has four goal contributions in his last three UEL outings (G2, A2), while eight of his last ten scoring appearances at club level came in away matches.

Plzeň look to have no new injury concerns, while Fredrik Aursnes is doubtful and Leandro Barreiro is unavailable for Benfica.

For all the latest team news, please check the Flashscore match centre.

Betting Analysis

As Benfica have won all four of their UEL league-phase games by at least two goals, there could be value in backing Benfica -1.5 in the handicap market.

FLASHSCORE PREVIEW

Royale Union Saint-Gilloise are flying high in the UEFA Europa League (UEL), and matchday four sees the Belgian outfit host Polish champions Lech Poznań, who are struggling on the continent.

Match News and Current Form

Royale Union are yet to taste defeat in 90 minutes in any competition this term (W14, D6), leading the way in the Belgian Pro League and faring very well in the UEL (W3, D1). David Hubert’s side have won seven games on the spin, and have already matched the club’s joint-best unbeaten run in the main draw of major European competitions (W4, D1), creating the opportunity to write their names into the history books outright here. Les Unionistes haven't made it out of the UEL group/league phase since the 2022/23 campaign, but look well-placed to achieve automatic qualification for the knockouts this time around.

Lech made it back-to-back domestic title triumphs in 2025/26 and sit top of the Ekstraklasa table again having lost just one league game this term (W11, D2), but haven't maintained anywhere near that form on the continent. Niels Frederiksen’s side collected a point at home against Sunderland (1-1), but have lost their other three UEL matches by at least a two-goal margin and sit second-bottom of the league phase table. The Railwaymen’s fortunes must change swiftly if they are to stand any chance of progressing into the knockouts, but having lost five away games on the spin in the main draw of the UEL, it looks unlikely that will happen here.

Head-to-Head History

This is the pair’s first meeting and Royale Union’s first-ever H2H with a Polish side. Lech are yet to draw in nine H2Hs against Belgian clubs (W4, L5).

Hot Stats and Streaks

Royale Union haven't conceded over 1.5 goals in any of their four UEL games this season.

Royale Union have taken under 4.5 corners in each of this term’s four UEL games.

Eight of Lech’s last 11 competitive games saw both teams score.

Lech have conceded a competition-high three penalties in this season’s UEL league phase.

Key Players to Watch and Missing Players

Besfort Zeneli scored both of Royale Union’s goals as they beat Celta Vigo 2-1 last time out in the UEL, and has registered four goal involvements in their last seven matches (G3, A1). Attempting to keep him out here, Lech goalkeeper Mateusz Lis has made a competition-high 29 saves in this season’s UEL league phase.

Royale Union remain without long-term absentees Kevin Mac Allister and Mateo Biondić. Lech’s lengthy injury list includes João Moutinho and Patrik Wålemark, with a late check needed on team-mate Pablo Rodríguez.

Betting Analysis

The hosts’ form has been remarkable, and if they perform as well as they have been doing in this season’s UEL, Royale Union to win both halves looks a likely outcome.

FLASHSCORE PREVIEW

Ararat-Armenia travel to Salzburg still looking for their first point in a major European fixture, but Armenian sides shouldering a terrible record against Austrian opposition hints at more misery here.

Match News and Current Form

After going down against Austria Vienna on Sunday, Salzburg have now lost two of their last three competitive outings, leaving them playing catch-up in both the Austrian Bundesliga and UEFA Europa League (UEL). Eating up the ground on the sides above them here is far from a foregone conclusion, as after posting a three-match winless UEL run (D1, L2), Salzburg have now been beaten in 11 of their last 16 matches in this competition (W4, D1). Home seems like as good a place as any to add to that win tally though, as despite going down 4-0 to AC Milan in the last European outing they hosted, they had won four in a row prior, while they also won their last two competitive home matches by an 8-1 aggregate scoreline. 

Despite losing just one of their 13 domestic league games so far this season (W10, D2), including a 2-1 away win on Friday, Ararat-Armenia are the only team in this season’s UEL to have lost all four group stage games. It was the last one which will have hurt the most for Tulipa’s side, who led 2-1 in second-half stoppage time against Torreense and still lost 3-2, putting them on the brink of becoming the first team to concede 3+ goals in their first five major European games since Dukla Banská Bystrica from 1984 to 2004. Defence has long-since been their kryptonite in Europe, as the Armenians have failed to keep a clean sheet in any of their last nine continental away matches and unsurprisingly arrive in Austria without a win in any of their last seven games on the road in Europe (D1, L6).

Head-to-Head History

Armenian sides have lost all five previous European meetings with Austrian teams by an aggregate score of 16-0, which includes Salzburg’s 10-0 success over two legs against Urartu in the 2008/09 UEFA Cup qualifiers.

Hot Stats and Streaks

Only one of Salzburg’s last six European games saw both teams score.

Salzburg have failed to keep a clean sheet in their last seven competitive matches (W4, D1, L2).

Ararat-Armenia have conceded before the 25th minute in their four league phase matches this season.

Only two sides have collected more UEL league phase yellow cards than Ararat-Armenia (13) this season.

Key Players to Watch and Missing Players

Jesper Lindstrøm tends to be in the thick of the action when he’s involved from the off, contributing to at least one goal (G2, A2) or being booked (Y1) in his last four competitive starts. Bruno Wilson has scored two of Ararat-Armenia’s four goals in this competition with both coming after half-time, but another goal could be a negative omen given his last four club goals came in defeats.

Salzburg appear to have no new injury worries, while João Bravim is suspended for Ararat-Armenia.

For all the latest team news, please check the Flashscore match centre.

Betting Analysis

Ararat-Armenia can’t buy a win in the UEL, so backing Salzburg to win and score 2+ goals given their scoring exploits at home seems a smart avenue to go down.

Author: Tom Penn

FLASHSCORE PREVIEW

Two sides locked on five points in the UEFA Europa League (UEL) clash as Crystal Palace and Real Sociedad each try to strengthen their claim to progress deeper in the competition. 

Match News and Current Form

European football is likely a welcome distraction for the Crystal Palace faithful, who have watched their side fall to four straight winless games (D1, L3) under two different managers. Seeking a first win at the second time of asking, new Palace manager Thomas Frank fell to a 3-2 defeat on his debut against Coventry on Saturday, but will now hope to emulate his success as Spurs boss in his last European league phase (W5, D2, L1). Returning to south London should aid his cause, as not only did four of Frank’s five European wins come in home games, but the Eagles are unbeaten in each of their last eight major European games at Selhurst Park since October 2025 (W5, D3). 

Locked on five points with Palace at the lower end of the pre-round qualification picture, Sociedad will make the journey to England sitting pretty in fifth place in La Liga in spite of a 3-2 defeat to Racing Santander on Sunday. Failing to win three of the last four competitive matches is a concern (W1, D1, L2), and it’s far from guaranteed that run will improve here given Pellegrino Matarazzo has won just two of his eight managerial games in the UEL proper (D4, L2). Three of those four career draws came after Matarazzo’s men scored first, so emulating their multi-goal return from their latest UEL trip, a 6-0 win over Lillestrøm, could be crucial.

Head-to-Head History

This is the first meeting between the sides and only Palace’s second encounter against Spanish opponents since beating Rayo Vallecano in the 2025/26 Conference League final. Sociedad have failed to win in all but one of their 11 H2Hs against English sides (D3, L7) after a 2-1 defeat against Bournemouth earlier this campaign. 

Hot Stats and Streaks

Crystal Palace have conceded first in three of their four league phase outings this season. 

Crystal Palace have scored six of their nine UEL goals this term after half-time. 

Seven of Sociedad’s last eight European matches saw both teams score. 

The half-time result was replicated at full-time in three of Sociedad’s four league phase matches.

Key Players to Watch and Missing Players

Daichi Kamada has contributed to 16 goals across his last 25 UEL appearances (G13, A3) and arrives here in solid form for Palace, scoring in two of his last three league phase games. Sergio Gómez has provided a notable threat from left back this season, assisting in La Liga over the weekend while scoring all three of his goals this season in the UEL. 

Adam Wharton is suspended for Palace after his red card in the last round, while Sociedad’s Ander Barrenetxea awaits surgery for his hamstring injury. 

For all the latest team news, please check the Flashscore match centre.

Betting Analysis

Sociedad’s concerning return against English sides could continue here, and backing Palace to benefit from a new manager bounce with a home win could prove sensible. 

Author: Matthew Billon

FLASHSCORE PREVIEW

Ferencváros will be gunning for top spot in the league phase of the UEFA Europa League (UEL) when they host an improving Celje, who achieved a surprise win in their last overseas trip. 

Match News and Current Form

Heading into matchday five, Ferencváros are one of three teams in this season’s UEL main draw with four wins from four games after a surprise 2-0 triumph at AC Milan, which was one of two victories that they have already secured as underdogs in this league phase campaign. The 36-time Hungarian top-flight champions are now pursuing a fifth consecutive major European main draw win for the first time since May 1968 and have the long-term form to suggest that they should achieve that feat. Their domestic league aspirations took a hit at the weekend when they lost 3-1 to Győr, but with that being their first competitive defeat in 23 matches (W15, D7), and back-to-back losses last coming in February, it could just be an anomaly. 

Celje could be in the mood to cause another upset of their own though after they won 3-2 at Sturm Graz on matchday four, picking up their first-ever UEL league phase victory in the process. That was the second game of an ongoing five-match winning streak for the Counts across all competitions, their longest since an eight-game one between March and April, with a clean sheet at the weekend another promising sign. Shutouts have been especially difficult to come by for Celje in European football this season, as they have earned only one in ten such matches (W3, D3, L4), although they have lost just two of their five away games in that run of results (W1, D2).

Head-to-Head History

Ferencváros have not met a Slovenian team since the country declared independence in 1991, while Celje have never played a side from Hungary.

Hot Stats and Streaks

Ferencváros’ last seven matches were decided by a 2+ goal margin.

Ferencváros’ last ten goals all came after half-time.

Six of Celje’s last nine losses saw them score.

Four of Celje’s last five matches produced over 2.5 goals.

Key Players to Watch and Missing Players

Ferencváros star Kristoffer Zachariassen has been one of the UEL’s standout performers this season, having been directly involved in more goals (G3, A3) than any other player after four matchdays. Benjamin Verbič struck at Sturm for Celje and followed that goal up with one at the weekend, the tenth of his last 12 strikes to arrive after half-time.

Ferencváros’ Bamidele Yusuf is serving a two-game ban after being sent off against Milan, while Celje don't seem to have any fresh absentees. 

For all the latest team news, please check the Flashscore match centre.

Betting Analysis

Both teams’ recent games have featured plenty of goals, so over 2.5 goals in this encounter looks pretty likely.

FLASHSCORE PREVIEW

Hoffenheim will look to take a step closer to UEFA Europa League (UEL) knockout round qualification and inflict more misery on an out-of-form Sturm Graz side who remain in terrible away European form.

Match News and Current Form

With just one win from their opening four league phase matches (D1, L2), Hoffenheim’s hopes of qualifying for the knockout rounds remain in the balance. Their 1-1 draw away to Crystal Palace on the last matchday may look like a strong return on paper, but conceding a 91st-minute equaliser against ten men left a bitter taste and forms part of a run which has seen them win just one of their last five competitive outings (D1, L3). That sole victory did at least come the last time they played on home soil and they also won their last UEL home match, meaning they are now looking to post successive UEL home wins for the first time since December 2020.

Visiting Sturm Graz have an identical record to Hoffenheim after four rounds (W1, D1, L2) as they look to play knockout European football for the first time since 2023/24. Such a return mainly owes to their goal-shy nature so far, netting just three goals in total in European action which, when coupled with a failure to keep a clean sheet in over a month (D2, L4), makes for an unwanted combination. Snapping that winless run here looks a tall order for a side in the midst of an ongoing nine-match losing streak across away major European fixtures, but they can perhaps cling to the fact their last competitive victory did come in this competition.   

Head-to-Head History

This will be the first meeting between these sides, though Sturm Graz are winless in five away European games against German clubs (D1, L4).

Hot Stats and Streaks

Hoffenheim have kept just two clean sheets across their last 15 competitive matches.

Only one side has won more corners in this season’s UEL than Hoffenheim (31).

Five of Sturm Graz’s last six matches have seen both teams score.

Sturm Graz have faced 5+ shots on target in three of their four UEL games this season.

Key Players to Watch and Missing Players

Fisnik Asllani both scored and assisted in his last home appearance for Hoffenheim, with six of his last eight club strikes now coming on home soil. Oumar Diakité has 12 goals across 13 games for Sturm Graz this season, the last four of which came in losing causes.

Hoffenheim are without a number of first-teamers including midfielder Nathan De Cat, while Sturm Graz are still without first-choice goalkeeper Daniil Khudyakov. 

For all the latest team news, please check the Flashscore match centre. 

Betting Analysis

Given Sturm Graz’s poor recent form and Hoffenheim’s strong home record of late, backing the home win and both teams to score could prove a solid choice. 

Author: Nathan Evans

FLASHSCORE PREVIEW

Juventus will want to cement their place in the top eight of this season’s UEFA Europa League (UEL) league phase when they host an Omonia side who are chasing progression themselves. 

Match News and Current Form

Juventus entered this round of the league phase in fifth place after three wins and a draw from their four matches, culminating in a 2-1 win away to AZ Alkmaar last round. Since then they hit the road again in a 2-2 draw with Fiorentina before emphatically beating Venezia 4-0 at home at the weekend in what would’ve been a confidence boosting performance. That result means the Old Lady have won three of their last four matches (D1) and their last two at the Allianz Stadium without conceding, meaning optimism will be high they can extend their unbeaten record at home in the UEL (W6, D9).

After naming the oldest starting XI on average in the UEL this season (29 years, 347 days) with at least six players aged 30+ in all four lineups, Omonia’s experienced squad is unlikely to be intimidated in this match against one of the European greats. That experience seemed to have handsomely paid off when the Cypriots won their opening two league phase matches, but subsequent 4-1 and 3-1 losses to Benfica and Nijmegen respectively see them enter this round in 18th place. Despite their two recent setbacks, manager Henning Berg seems to have instilled an edge of fearlessness into Omonia, who’ve gone out and scored in nine of their last 11 European matches regardless of location. 

Head-to-Head History

These sides have met four times in the past which contributes to Juventus’ 100% winning record against Cypriot teams (W7) and Omonia’s 100% losing rate against Italian sides (L6).

Hot Stats and Streaks

Juventus’ last six European matches featured over 2.5 goals.

Just one of Juve’s last six home games saw both teams score.

None of Omonia’s last eight European matches saw them trail at half-time.

Omonia’s last six away fixtures were decided by a 2+ goal margin.

Key Players to Watch and Missing Players

Juventus’ Nick Woltemade has either scored or assisted in all four UEL games this season (G3, A2), and he’ll be confident he can get on the scoresheet again since four of his last six goals came at home. Omonia’s best route to goal seems to be through Loïs Diony who has scored in his last four matches, with all four goals arriving in the opening 25 minutes and serving as the match opener. 

Kerim Alajbegović went down for Juve at the weekend, joining Pierre Kalulu as the latest additions to their injury list, while Omonia seemingly have no new injuries to contend with.

For all the latest team news, please check the Flashscore match centre.

Betting Analysis

The hosts should prevail but it’ll prove difficult to keep Omonia quiet, hence a Juventus win with both teams to score makes a lot of sense. 

Author: Peter Stavrinou

FLASHSCORE PREVIEW

Lyon will hope to continue their impressive home record and move closer to the top eight in the UEFA Europa League (UEL) league phase when a winless Lillestrøm visit Parc Olympique Lyonnais on matchday five.

Match News and Current Form

Lyon won 1-0 against Lille last weekend in Ligue 1, making it a winning start for new manager Carlos Vicens, although that was just their second win across six matches (D1, L3), including winning only one point across the last two UEL matchdays. Those continental results dampened spirits after they started the league phase with back-to-back wins, and restoring that momentum could see Les Gones move into the top eight, as they are behind only on goal difference ahead of this round. A five-match winning run at this venue should boost Vicens’ hopes of not only winning on his home bow, but also extending Lyon’s run of five wins from their last five UEL home games.

Lillestrøm won 2-0 at the weekend in the Eliteserien for a fifth victory in their last six matches (L1). That domestic run masks their deficiencies in Europe, as they remain winless in the league phase (D1, L3) and have spent 264 minutes and 47 seconds trailing in this competition. Hans Erik Ødegaard’s men look to change that script here, arriving on the back of three consecutive away wins, each with a clean sheet, but replicating that on the road looks a big challenge, as the Norwegians have historically struggled in UEFA competitions, with just one win across their last 12 away matches (D5, L6).

Head-to-Head History

These teams have never met in European competition before, and while Lyon are unbeaten in all four UEFA games against Norwegian clubs (W3, D1), Lillestrøm are winless in their five UEFA matches against French opposition (D1, L4).

Hot Stats and Streaks

Lyon have scored 2+ goals in eight of their last ten home UEFA matches.

Seven of the last 11 goals in Lyon’s UEL campaign were scored in the second half.

Seven of Lillestrøm’s last ten competitive goals were scored after half-time.

Only four of Lillestrøm’s last 18 competitive away games saw both teams score.

Key Players to Watch and Missing Players

Only two players have created more chances in the UEL this season than Keito Nakamura (12), and his three direct goal contributions (G1, A2) have featured in two Lyon wins in this competition. Thomas Lehne Olsen could be looking for a late impact as his three UEL goals this season have all arrived beyond the 75th minute, each serving as the last goal of the match.

Lyon avoided any new major injury concerns last weekend, while questions remain over Camil Jebara’s availability for Lillestrøm.

For all the latest team news, please check the Flashscore match centre.

Betting Analysis

With Lyon's strong home form, backing a home win looks a safe selection to include in multiples.

FLASHSCORE PREVIEW

Both may be struggling domestically, but NEC Nijmegen and Rennes are performing admirably in the UEFA Europa League (UEL) and can bolster their qualification chances with a win here. 

Match News and Current Form

Nijmegen’s first appearance in the main draw of a European competition since 2008/09 got off to a rocky start with a heavy defeat at Juventus, but a three-match unbeaten run since (W2, D1) has seen them score seven goals across a pair of impressive wins over Dinamo Zagreb and Omonia. Dick Schreuder’s men have earned all seven of their points from a losing position thus far, but that resilience has largely been absent at home where they’ve won just one of their last 11 games within regulation time (D6, L4). A 4-1 defeat to PSV here on Saturday left NEC in the bottom half of the Eredivisie, placing even greater importance on their European fortunes.

Rennes have made slower progress this UEL campaign, as although they’ve remained unbeaten, three draws have undermined their progress. Losing just two of their 21 major European group/league phase matches since the 2021/22 season (W11, D8) highlights their comfort in this setting, but Franck Haise’s men are chasing improvement after a four-match winless run in all competitions (D2, L2) which has dropped them into mid-table in Ligue 1. They’re especially keen for an upturn on the road where Rennes are winless in six (D3, L3) and have won just once since April.

Head-to-Head History

This is NEC’s first game against a French team, while Rennes have lost just one of their four meetings with Dutch teams (W2, D1).

Hot Stats and Streaks

NEC have been behind at half-time in five of their last six European matches. 

Nine of NEC’s last ten games saw both teams score.

Just two of Rennes’ last ten European matches were decided by a 2+ goal margin.

Four of Rennes’ last five away matches produced over 3.5 goals.

Key Players to Watch and Missing Players

NEC’s Bryan Linssen is a man in form with three goals in as many games, all of which came after half-time in home games. Boulaye Dia has netted six goals in his last seven games for club and country, while four of his last five for Rennes came in the first half.

Nijmegen defender Perr Schuurs has not featured since going off injured on matchday four, while Rennes’ Valentin Rongier and defender Przemysław Frankowski are unlikely to feature.

For all the latest team news, please check the Flashscore match centre.

Betting Analysis

These two usually deliver entertainment, making the over 3.5 total goals market rather attractive.

FLASHSCORE PREVIEW

OFI Crete and Anderlecht enter matchday five of this season’s UEFA Europa League (UEL) side by side in the league-phase table, with both teams having won their last game in the competition. 

Match News and Current Form

OFI sit 16th ahead of this round of fixtures, only one place behind Anderlecht on goal difference, after beating Hapoel Be’er Sheva 2-0 on matchday four. That was their second clean-sheet win of the league phase (L2), which is perhaps surprising given that pre-round, Christos Kontis’ men have faced the most shots (95) and the second-most shots on target (33) in the UEL league phase. That approach has proven to be to their detriment at home, where OFI have won just one of their last four competitive games, but with five of their last six victories at Pankritio Stadium being accompanied by a clean sheet, defence is likely to be the bedrock of any potential success here.

Anderlecht have corrected the course of their UEL campaign with successive wins to nil across the last two rounds, and the Belgian outfit have the chance here to make it three consecutive European main-draw victories without conceding for the first time since November 2011. The most recent of those positive results came against Salzburg (2-0), with that win forming part of an ongoing four-match unbeaten run (W3, D1) for the Purple and White, which includes their 1-0 victory over Leuven on Sunday. Now looking towards emulating their best-ever performance in this competition from ten seasons ago when they reached the quarter-finals, Anderlecht may have to overcome some travelling demons as they’ve lost three of their last five competitive away games (W1, D1). 

Head-to-Head History

These sides have never played each other before, while OFI have never faced a Belgian team. Anderlecht have already gone up against a Greek outfit this season, beating PAOK 4-2 on aggregate in UEL qualifying. 

Hot Stats and Streaks

OFI have attempted the fewest shots (26) in this league phase.

Just one of OFI’s six European matches this term saw both teams score.

The team scoring first won each of Anderlecht’s last eight UEL games.

Pre-round, Anderlecht have suffered the third-most fouls in the UEL main draw this season (63).

Key Players to Watch and Missing Players

Taxiarchis Fountas scored OFI’s second against Be’er Sheva, the seventh successive goal of his to arrive before the hour mark. Marten Winkler was Anderlecht’s second goalscorer against Salzburg, meaning that he has now been on the winning side in his last 12 goalscoring appearances.

OFI’s Kenan Kodro and Krešimir Krizmanić missed their 2-0 loss to Panathinaikos at the weekend through injury, while Anderlecht don’t seem to have any fresh absentees. 

For all the latest team news, please check the Flashscore match centre.

Betting Analysis

Given how close these two sides are to each other in the table, backing a draw seems logical here.

FLASHSCORE PREVIEW

Sparta Prague and AZ go to battle for a second successive season, with the hosts in greater need of a strong result in this UEFA Europa League (UEL) clash given their dire form.

Match News and Current Form

A run of one win in nine matches across all competitions (D4, L4) and none in their last five (D2, L3) led Sparta Prague to sack manager Brian Priske and sporting director Tomáš Rosický this week. A whopping 13 points off the title pace domestically, Sparta have also struggled in Europe, failing to win any of their last three league phase games (D1, L2) after emerging victorious on matchday one. One of those defeats came at home to Bournemouth last time out in the UEL, and puts the Czech side at risk of losing successive home matches in this competition for the very first time here.

To inflict that fate, AZ will need to win back-to-back away games in this competition for the first time since December 2006. They were winless in their nine UEL trips prior to matchday three’s 4-0 thrashing of Ararat-Armenia, and have since been beaten by Juventus, although they remain comfortably inside the top 24 (W2, L2). The Cheese Farmers are therefore well placed to match their run to the last 16 of this competition from 2024/25, and confidence will have been boosted by firing in nine goals across a pair of Eredivisie wins since that Juventus defeat.

Head-to-Head History

AZ won both H2Hs in the last 16 of the Conference League last season, including a 4-0 victory on this ground, stretching their unbeaten record in European games against Czech teams to ten matches in the process (W6, D4).

Hot Stats and Streaks

All six of the goals Sparta conceded in the league phase came after half-time.

Just five teams were given more yellow cards across the first four matchdays than Sparta (11).

The team who scored first went on to win all four of AZ’s league phase matches this term.

Five red cards have been shown across AZ’s last seven games in all competitions.

Key Players to Watch and Missing Players

Andrew Irving has directly contributed to seven goals for Sparta this season (G3, A4), with all three of his strikes coming in home wins which saw them net 3+ times overall. After failing to score in his first 18 major European appearances for AZ, Mexx Meerdink has netted in his last three, though only two AZ players have ever done so in four.

Sparta’s Tobias Guddal is suspended, while Hugo Sochůrek and Santiago Eneme missed their weekend defeat. AZ are without Lewis Schouten, Kees Smit and Weslley Patati.

For all the latest team news, please check the Flashscore match centre.

Betting Analysis

Sparta’s crisis and the visitors’ scoring form of late make AZ at a -1 handicap a tempting route.

FLASHSCORE PREVIEW

Sunderland aim to build on an upturn in domestic form in this UEFA Europa League (UEL) clash against Jagiellonia, who are fighting to stay in play-off contention and avoid making unwanted history.

Match News and Current Form

Sunderland were unbeaten in Europe this term before losing 2-0 to Dinamo Zagreb on matchday four, but a win here would put them on the brink of reaching at least the knockout play-off stage (W2, D1, L1). They’ve kept back-to-back Premier League clean sheets since that defeat (W1, D1), and the Black Cats’ defensive organisation is especially important in Europe given that they’ve converted a mere 4.8% of their shots in the league phase. Losing just one of their last four competitive home games is more encouraging for Régis Le Bris’ side (W2, D1), although scoring under 1.5 goals in eight of their nine matches at the Stadium of Light this term points to long-term attacking deficiencies. 

Jagiellonia also lost their matchday four game, going down 1-0 to Levski Sofia, but that was their third defeat of the league phase (W1), leaving them outside of the qualification positions. Having lost their last two European games without scoring, Adrian Siemieniec’s side risk suffering three consecutive major European defeats for the first time, while Saturday’s 3-1 league loss to Cracovia hardly helped their preparations. Jaga will also have to cope without their travelling supporters following a UEFA ban as they try to avoid losing three successive away games in Europe for the first time.

Head-to-Head History

These two sides have never met, but Sunderland have already played Polish opponents in the league phase, drawing 1-1 at Lech Poznań on matchday three. Jagiellonia have never played an English side, but are unbeaten against British opposition (W1, D1).

Hot Stats and Streaks

There were fewer than ten corners in each of Sunderland’s last eight fixtures in all competitions.

Eight of Sunderland’s nine home games this season produced under 2.5 goals.

Three Jagiellonia players were booked in all four of their league phase games this term.

All four of Jagiellonia’s away UEL games this term produced exactly one second-half goal.

Key Players to Watch and Missing Players

Trai Hume has been booked in two of Sunderland’s last three matches, while he received a yellow card between the 20th and 60th minute in three of their four UEL games this term. Nik Prelec’s goal for Jagiellonia against Cracovia on Saturday was a third in his last five appearances, with each of his last four strikes coming in games producing at least four total goals.

Sunderland remain without Dan Ballard, Brian Brobbey and Granit Xhaka, while Jagiellonia don’t appear to have any fresh injury concerns.

For all the latest team news, please check the Flashscore match centre.

Betting Analysis

Sunderland’s poor conversion rate despite creating several chances in Europe, combined with Jagiellonia’s struggles in the league phase, make backing under 2.5 goals in this one a viable choice.

Author: John Pennington

FLASHSCORE PREVIEW

Second-tier Portuguese side Torreense have defied the odds in this season’s UEFA Europa League (UEL) and will look to continue their impressive campaign against a Celtic side who picked up their first win in the last round.

Match News and Current Form

Few expected much from Torreense in the UEL aside from them making up the numbers, but two wins from their first four league phase outings (L2) have placed them firmly in top-24 contention. A dramatic 3-2 victory over Ararat-Armenia on matchday four has been followed up by back-to-back domestic defeats, the first of which left them close to the relegation zone in Liga Portugal 2, while Sunday’s defeat to Benfica ended their Taça de Portugal title defence. Playing away from their home ground due to their stadium not meeting UEFA regulations could be deemed a hindrance here, but having won just two of the eight matches they’ve hosted at any venue this term (D2, L4), that may not play a big role. 

After opening their campaign with three successive defeats, Celtic picked up their first UEL victory when they beat Beşiktaş 3-2 in the last round. The Bhoys are still a point adrift of the top 24 pre-round, but they’re clear at the top of the Scottish Premiership following Saturday’s 4-1 win against St Mirren. It's easy to see why they’re struggling in Europe as their 11 goals conceded is one of the highest such tallies in the league phase, and that’s been an ongoing trend for Celtic on the European scene, as since the start of 2020/21 they’ve conceded more goals in major European competition than any other side (116).

Head-to-Head History

Portuguese teams are unbeaten in their last five UEL matches against Scottish opposition (W3, D2), while Celtic haven’t won away to Portuguese opposition since April 2003 (L5).

Hot Stats and Streaks

All four of Torreense’s league phase games produced over 2.5 goals.

Torreense have conceded seven of their nine goals in the league phase after half-time.

Celtic have scored five of their six league phase goals this term in the second half. 

Celtic haven’t led a league phase game at half-time this season (D2, L2).

Key Players to Watch and Missing Players

Torreense’s Musa Drammeh has been amongst the goals lately, netting at the weekend and also their late winner against Ararat-Armenia - 11 of his last 12 club goals arrived after half-time. Camilo Durán was Celtic’s hero against Beşiktaş and has a knack for scoring big goals as he’s netted the decisive goal on six of his last nine scoring appearances. 

Adama Baradji remains sidelined for Torreense, while Celtic’s Mika Baur missed their weekend win against St Mirren. 

For all the latest team news, please check the Flashscore match centre.

Betting Analysis

Picking a winner is tough here, but second-half trends of these sides hint that backing Celtic to score after half-time could be a good approach to take.

Author: Chris Wilson

FLASHSCORE PREVIEW

Kairat Almaty will still be pursuing their maiden win in the main draw of any major European competition when they host continental debutants Mjällby, who are unbeaten in the UEFA Conference League so far this season. 

Match News and Current Form

Kairat overachieved in a 1-1 draw away to Atalanta on matchday three of the competition but remained winless in 17 European main draw fixtures (D5, L12) and have collected just two points during the league phase of this season’s Conference League. That was the most recent assignment for the out-of-season Kazakhstani side, who can take heart from the fact that they have scored in all three of their league phase matches so far this term after going scoreless in four consecutive Champions or Europa League qualifiers. That phase of their continental journey saw them record the first two of three consecutive continental home defeats, during which they conceded nine goals and scored only one.

Mjällby also ended up in the Conference League after unsuccessful attempts to qualify for the Champions and Europa Leagues earlier this season, but they have since fared considerably better than their upcoming opponents in the Conference League (W2, D1). Their latest win in this league phase - 2-0 over Borac Banja Luka - means that all three of their victories in Europe this term have been accompanied by a clean sheet, complementing the one goal conceded across their last three domestic matches. Mjällby’s next achievement to tick off is their inaugural away win in all European football, something they have not achieved in four attempts (D2, L2).

Head-to-Head History

The only previous meeting between a Kazakhstani and a Swedish team saw Astana beat AIK 4-1 on aggregate in 2014/15 UEL qualifying. 

Hot Stats and Streaks

The last five goals scored or conceded by Kairat in any competition came after half-time. 

Kairat won only one of their last four competitive matches when scoring the opening goal (D3). 

Ten of Mjällby’s last 11 competitive games featured under 2.5 goals. 

Mjällby’s last eight UEFA matches all produced 0-0 half-time scores.

Key Players to Watch and Missing Players

Marc Gual’s match opener for Kairat against Atalanta was the fifth time in his last six scoring appearances that he has netted the club’s first goal of the game. Villiam Granath put Mjällby in front against Malmö on Saturday in a 1-1 draw, recording the seventh successive time that he has avoided being on the losing side when scoring (W5, D2). 

Kairat do not seem to have any fresh absentees, while Mjällby pair Jacob Bergström and Ludvig Tidstrand went off injured against Malmö at the weekend.

For all the latest team news, please check the Flashscore match centre.

Betting Analysis

Given the complete absence of first-half goals in Mjällby’s last eight European games, 0-0 at half-time seems like a wise selection here. 

Author: Alex Bowmer

FLASHSCORE PREVIEW

Ajax are in blistering form at present and look to take the next step on the road to knockout football in the UEFA Conference League when they host a Thun side hoping a win in the last round can help them turn a corner. 

Match News and Current Form

Ajax suffered a shock Conference League matchday one defeat to Hajduk Split (2-1), but that is their only loss in 12 competitive games (W8, D3), having responded with wins over Atalanta (2-0) and Midtjylland (6-1) in this competition. Having scored six goals in a European encounter for the first time this century earlier this month, the Dutch side are unsurprisingly overwhelming favourites to continue their 100% continental home record this season (W4) in this fixture. Tightening up defensively is a priority though for the Amsterdam outfit, who have kept just one clean sheet in their last 20 European matches no matter the venue. 

Thun clinched a first Swiss Super League title last term, but summer appointment Gian-Luca Privitelli has failed to impress after being tasked with overseeing the club’s first-ever Conference League campaign. Privitelli’s side have struggled desperately in domestic action, losing eight of their 14 league games (W4, D2), as well as their first two matches in this competition against Twente and Hajduk (both 1-0). A 3-1 win over Hearts earlier this month did end Thun’s seven-game main draw losing run in Europe and has given them some hope of finishing in the top 24, but they have never won back-to-back matches on the continent in a group/league phase.

Head-to-Head History

Ajax won both previous H2Hs by a two-goal margin, with those two meetings taking place in the 2005/06 UEFA Champions League group phase.

Hot Stats and Streaks

Eleven of Ajax’s last 12 European matches saw both teams score and featured over 2.5 goals.

Ajax have received just three yellow cards in the main draw of the Conference League this term.

Thun’s last five games each saw both teams score and featured over 3.5 goals.

Thun have committed a competition-high 68 main draw fouls this season.

Key Players to Watch and Missing Players

Three of Owen Wijndal’s four goal involvements for Ajax this term have come in the Conference League (G2, A1), including a goal and an assist against Midtjylland. Three of Nils Reichmuth’s four yellow cards this season have come in Europe, with the 24-year-old receiving a booking in both of Thun’s last two games in this competition.

Ajax might be without Viktor Tsygankov, while Caio Henrique and Jorthy Mokio may also not feature here due to injury. Neither Mattias Käit nor Furkan Dursun were in Thun’s squad for their 3-2 loss to Young Boys at the weekend. 

Betting Analysis

Ajax have shown that they are capable of taking teams apart, and if they are in the mood again here, over 3.5 home goals seems realistic.

Author: Ben Olawumi

FLASHSCORE PREVIEW

Brann will be looking to continue their finest European season in more than 50 years by denying Aarhus their first league phase win of this UEFA Conference League season. 

Match News and Current Form

Brann are almost certainly now out of contention to qualify for European football next season via the 2026 Norwegian Eliteserien and can now turn the majority of their attention to what has so far been an excellent Conference League campaign. They began matchday four in sixth place as one of ten clubs yet to be defeated, with their two wins and one draw their best start to any major European competition since the 1973/74 Cup Winners’ Cup. That includes a win over Lincoln Red Imps in their only league phase game at home this season, forming part of a record of seven wins from their last ten home fixtures (L3) in all competitions. 

Goal difference was the only thing keeping winless Aarhus (D1, L2) inside the top-24 at the halfway point of the league phase. They’re at a fascinating part of their season, having completed two-thirds of their Danish Superliga campaign and teetering between the championship and relegation groups in the table. A run of just two competitive defeats since the middle of September (W6, D4) affords some optimism here, but both defeats did come on the road, where they have won only two of their last 12 games in all competitions (D3, L7) and lost eight of their nine continental games played this century (W1).

Head-to-Head History

This is Brann’s second meeting with Danish opposition after equalising three times in a 3-3 draw with Midtjylland in last season’s UEL. Aarhus last met a Norwegian side in the 1960/61 European Cup. 

Hot Stats and Streaks

Seven of Brann’s last nine games in all competitions produced over 2.5 goals.

Eight of Brann’s nine continental games this season saw both teams score. 

Five of Aarhus’ last six competitive matches saw the winning team score exactly two goals.

Eight of Aarhus’ 11 continental defeats this century were by a 2+ goal margin. 

Key Players to Watch and Missing Players

Kristall Máni Ingason continues to be in stellar form for Brann, scoring or assisting in each of his last six club games (G4, A2), whilst six of his last seven club goals came after half-time. Jacob Andersen is primed to record his maiden continental goal after striking in each of Aarhus’ two wins since their last Conference League match.

Jacob Sørensen leads Brann’s injury list, whilst Aarhus were missing Frederik Tingager and Janni Serra at the weekend.

For all the latest team news, please check the Flashscore match centre.

Betting Analysis

With these sides conceding only five goals combined in six league phase matches, this clash appears ripe for under 2.5 goals.

FLASHSCORE PREVIEW

Surprise Premier League title challengers Brighton look to continue balancing domestic and European commitments when they host a Universitatea Craiova side locked on seven points with the Seagulls in the UEFA Conference League. 

Match News and Current Form

Brighton received a harsh reality check on Sunday as they were beaten 2-0 by Hull, although they do remain Arsenal’s closest challengers at the Premier League summit. Dreams of winning a league title remain some way off yet, but the Seagulls are heavily fancied to win this competition, and it’s easy to see why having lost just twice across their last 14 competitive matches inside 90 minutes (W9, D3). Four successive wins to nil in major European home action only hint at their phenomenal run continuing here, and another such victory would see them become just the third English side this century to win five European home matches in a row without conceding. 

Univ. Craiova maintained their spot at the Romanian Superliga summit on Sunday with a 6-2 win against UTA Arad. The Romanian side are on a superb run of 15 unbeaten matches (W11, D4) and look well-placed to get one of the top-eight Conference League spots following back-to-back wins on matchdays two and three. They haven’t won three in a row in major European competition since a four-game stretch in the UEFA Cup in 1984, but if they’re to achieve that here, they’ll have to snap a six-match streak of alternating between losses and wins in Conference League away matches.

Head-to-Head History

Brighton have never faced Romanian opposition before, while Univ. Craiova won both prior H2Hs against English opposition, beating Leeds home and away in the 1979/80 UEFA Cup.

Hot Stats and Streaks

Brighton are the only side yet to concede in this season’s Conference League.

Only one of Brighton’s last ten home matches saw both teams score. 

Univ. Craiova have scored first in all three league phase games this term.

The two league phase goals Univ. Craiova conceded this season arrived after the 75th minute.

Key Players to Watch and Missing Players

Brighton’s Jack Hinshelwood could be a prime candidate to get on the scoresheet here having netted his last five goals in home games, all of which came in wins to nil. Univ. Craiova’s Ștefan Baiaram netted a brace on Sunday and may fancy his chances again here given his last four goals arrived before half-time in away games. 

Neither side appears to have any fresh concerns for this game. 

For all the latest team news, please check the Flashscore match centre.

Betting Analysis

This game represents a huge step-up in quality for the Romanian side, so backing Brighton to win to nil may not be a bad choice.

Author: Chris Wilson

FLASHSCORE PREVIEW

After respectable starts to their UEFA Conference League campaigns, unfancied duo Egnatia and Lincoln Red Imps look to strengthen their qualification bids on matchday four. 

Match News and Current Form

Egnatia opened their first major European campaign with successive draws, but a 2-0 loss to Universitatea Craiova in which they were reduced to ten men on matchday three means they’re outside the top 24. The Albanian side also had a player sent off in a 1-0 domestic defeat on Friday which cut their lead at the summit, so confidence may not be high ahead of this crucial fixture. Egnatia can certainly point to some stellar home form as reason for belief though, as they’re unbeaten on their own turf since April (W10, D3), although all three draws came in Europe. 

Lincoln Red Imps are a point better off than Egnatia (W1, L2), with the latest of those results being a priceless 1-0 victory over Hajduk Split which forms part of a five-match winning streak in all competitions. After losing their first seven major European matches, the Red Imps have now won three of their last eight (D1, L4), with their latest triumph also bringing around their first-ever clean sheet in the main draw of a UEFA competition. Lincoln now look to back that up on the road, but that looks a tall order for a side who’ve secured just one victory from their five European trips this season (D1, L3).

Head-to-Head History

This will be the first-ever meeting between an Albanian and a Gibraltarian side in European competition.

Hot Stats and Streaks

Egnatia failed to win any of the last three European games in which they scored first (D2, L1). 

Egnatia have conceded all four of their league phase goals this term before the 50th minute. 

Eight of Lincoln’s last ten competitive wins were accompanied by a clean sheet.

Seven of Lincoln’s last eight games featured over 2.5 goals. 

Key Players to Watch and Missing Players

Egnatia’s Alessandro Albanese scored in their last home victory, maintaining his 100% winning record when finding the net for the club (W14). Manu Toledano also boasts a perfect return of six victories when netting for Lincoln, though just one of his 12 strikes therein served to open the scoring. 

Egnatia will be without Eneo Bitri following his red card on matchday three, while Lincoln look to have no new availability issues. 

For all the latest team news, please check the Flashscore match centre.

Betting Analysis

Given Egnatia’s failure to turn recent bright European starts into victories, Egnatia to score first but Lincoln to win seems enticing here. 

Author: Alex Bowmer

FLASHSCORE PREVIEW

Hearts hope an extraordinary league win at the weekend can inspire a European revival as they host a so far perfect Monaco side on matchday four of the UEFA Conference League.

Match News and Current Form

Hearts’ 8-0 win over Dundee on Saturday was their biggest top-flight victory since 1957, ending a three-match losing streak in spectacular fashion. They’ve picked up just one Conference League point so far, but riding high on that remarkable result, Wouter Vrancken’s side will also come into this clash at Tynecastle Park encouraged by their improving home form in Europe. Hearts have lost just one of their last five major European fixtures here (W2, D2), a huge step up from losing each of their previous five without scoring.

Monaco are one of four sides to have opened this Conference League league phase with three successive wins, and victory here would see them win four major European games in a row for the first time since 1997. The Monégasques’ European consistency contrasts sharply with their struggles domestically as Filipe Luís’ side have failed to win any of their last six Ligue 1 games (D4, L2). Claiming a late 1-1 draw against Auxerre on Saturday showed their fighting spirit, which might offer them hope of boosting their record of winning just two of their last five European away fixtures (D2, L1).

Head-to-Head History

These two sides have never met previously. Hearts have one win from four previous meetings with French clubs (D1, L2), while Monaco are unbeaten in their last three visits to Scotland (W1, D2).

Hot Stats and Streaks

There was at least one goal in each half in all five of Hearts’ Conference League fixtures this term.

Seven of Hearts’ last nine home games produced over 2.5 goals and saw both teams score.

Just one Monaco player was booked across their last three fixtures.

Monaco scored at least twice in four of their last five European away games.

Key Players to Watch and Missing Players

Cláudio Braga has scored in five of his last six Hearts appearances, with six of his nine goals this term coming at home. Monaco’s Mathys Detourbet has scored three of his last four club goals between the tenth minute and half-time, including one on matchday three, a game in which he became the youngest Frenchman to score and assist in a major European game since Kylian Mbappé in October 2017.

Hearts have injury concerns over Stephen Kingsley and Tómas Magnússon. Aleksandr Golovin and Christian Mawissa missed Monaco’s Saturday game with injuries.

For all the latest team news, please check the Flashscore match centre.

Betting Analysis

If Hearts can build on their solid recent home form to pose Monaco some problems, then backing Hearts/Draw in the double chance market might be worth considering.

FLASHSCORE PREVIEW

With both still winless after the opening three matchdays, this clash between strugglers Iberia and Getafe looks crucial to both sides’ chances of progression in the UEFA Conference League.

Match News and Current Form

Iberia may be top-of-the-table domestically after a victory at the weekend, but they’re running out of time to extend their first-ever major European campaign. The Red Eagles were beaten 2-1 away at Copenhagen on matchday three to remain outside of the top 24 (D1, L2), but a one-point deficit means one of the competition’s biggest underdogs are still in contention to progress. A first-ever major European victory would go a long way to securing a place in the knockout stages, but this season’s showings indicate that Iberia have very little chance of doing so as they’ve failed to win any of their five European home matches this term inside 90 minutes (D3, L2).

Getafe arrive in Georgia on the back of three successive losses without scoring in all competitions, the first of which came against Brighton last time out in the Conference League. Handling domestic and European commitments has had a detrimental effect on both for the Azulones, who are also struggling towards the bottom of La Liga. Jose Bordalas’ men have lost seven of their nine competitive away games this season (W1, D1) and last won on the road against a top-flight team back in April, but the calibre of the opposition here should give them hope of ending their five-game winless run in major European fixtures (D1, L4).

Head-to-Head History

This will be a first-ever major European meeting between Georgian and Spanish sides.

Hot Stats and Streaks

Iberia’s last 14 competitive home wins came by a one-goal margin.

Only one side received more yellow cards than Iberia (10) across the first three matchdays.

Only one of Getafe’s last six away matches against top-flight opposition saw both teams score.

Getafe failed to score in ten of their last 11 away defeats.

Key Players to Watch and Missing Players

Jemali-Giorgi Jinjolava is bidding to become the first Georgian player to score multiple goals for a side from Georgia in a major European competition in over 20 years. Iván Azón was on target for Getafe on matchday two and has seen each of his last three goals serve as match openers, two of which came beyond the 75th minute.

Iberia look to have no fresh concerns, while Getafe’s Sebastián Boselli missed their weekend outing through injury.

For all the latest team news, please check the Flashscore match centre.

Betting Analysis

A meeting between two strugglers points to under 2.5 goals being a prime option, especially with shot-shy Getafe involved.

FLASHSCORE PREVIEW

An out-of-form Jablonec side will chase their first UEFA Conference League win of this season in the league phase when they host the marauding pre-round table-toppers Lugano.

Match News and Current Form

Jablonec entered matchday four of the league phase in 23rd place after losing their opener and following it up with two stalemates, the most recent of which saw them come from behind to draw 1-1 with Riga. Luboš Kozel’s men are at grave risk of dropping out of the qualification places here having won just one of their last nine matches in all competitions (D3, L5), including none of their last five at home (D3, L2). Even more worrying is the fact they haven’t won any of their last eight matches in major European competition (D5, L3), but Jablonec have a habit of always finding a way to be competitive when hosting overseas visitors, indicated by having not lost a single home game in the Conference League before (W1, D3).

Lugano were flying high at the top of the standings at the start of matchday four, underpinning their success with a free-scoring ruthlessness that has seen them win all three of their league phase matches in fine fashion. The visitors have now scored 3+ goals in each of their last four matches in the Conference League’s main draw (W4), making them the first Swiss side to do so in four consecutive games in the main draw of a European competition. That sets them up to become just the third Swiss team to win five in succession and travel requirements shouldn’t bother them here after they won an impressive 11 of their last 17 away games in all competitions (D5, L1).

Head-to-Head History

Jablonec will compete against a Swiss side for the first time here, while Lugano have won two and lost three of their five outings against Czech opposition.

Hot Stats and Streaks

Just two of Jablonec’s last 12 games were decided by a 2+ goal margin.

Just one of Jablonec’s last six home European matches saw both teams score.

Each of Lugano’s last 13 competitive matches featured over 2.5 goals.

The same half-time result was replicated come full-time in seven of Lugano’s last nine away fixtures.

Key Players to Watch and Missing Players

After he scored against Riga, Sebastian Nebyla will be feeling as though he is Jablonec’s lucky charm, having lost only one of his last 11 goalscoring appearances for his club (W9, D1). Lugano’s Daniel Dos Santos has shone recently with eight goal contributions in his last eight matches (G5, A3), making his presence felt early having recorded the match opener in four of his last five goalscoring outings. 

First-choice keeper Jan Hanuš remains absent for Jablonec, while Lugano will be without defender Hannes Delcroix.

For all the latest team news, please check the Flashscore match centre.

Betting Analysis

It’s hard to look past backing Lugano to win here as the momentum firmly lies with the visitors.

Author: Peter Stavrinou

FLASHSCORE PREVIEW

Lithuanian Toplyga champions Kauno Žalgiris will continue searching for their first points in the league phase of the UEFA Conference League when they take on Riga, who are looking for a new direction after parting ways with their longest-serving head coach.

Match News and Current Form

Kauno Žalgiris’ 4-1 loss to Transinvest earlier this month was inconsequential as they had already successfully defended their domestic title, but a fourth defeat in their last seven matches (W2, D1) could be of some concern. The hosts have had more than two weeks off to work out how to mount an unlikely European revival as one of two sides to have lost all three of their Conference League matches this edition, during what is their debut in a main draw of any major UEFA competition. Their slim hopes of reaching the knockout phase could depend on winning every remaining league phase game, and they will need a marked improvement on their home record to achieve that, having won just two of their last seven UEFA home games (D2, L3).

Losing the domestic title and then the Latvian Cup final proved to be the last straw for Riga’s Adrián Guľa, who left the club just four days before this fixture. Guľa led them to their own historic league phase debut and the visitors are also still searching for their maiden win after three 1-1 draws in the league phase. The Latvians are unbeaten across their last ten matches in Europe including qualifiers (W5, D5), but have struggled to replicate that form away from home. Riga have won only one of their last 13 away UEFA matches including qualifiers (D4, L8) although five victories from their last eight competitive trips (D2, L1) gives them hope of winning full points here.

Head-to-Head History

This will be the first ever major UEFA match between Lithuanian and Latvian clubs.

Hot Stats and Streaks

Thirteen of the last 18 goals scored in Kauno Žalgiris’ matches have come in the first half.

Kauno Žalgiris conceded 2+ goals in six of their last seven UEFA matches.

Six of Riga’s last seven UEFA matches produced under 2.5 total goals.

Riga conceded exactly two or three goals in eight of their last 11 away UEFA matches.

Key Players to Watch and Missing Players

Amine Benchaib could be the one driving Kauno Žalgiris’ revival in this competition, as he has scored 11 of his last 13 club goals at home. Iago Siqueira could spearhead Riga’s response with a late strike, as five of his last six club goals have come beyond the hour mark.

Both teams reportedly have no new major injury absences ahead of this matchday.

For all the latest team news, please check the Flashscore match centre.

Betting Analysis

Neither team has shown enough bite recently, so backing a draw could prove to be a handy choice.

FLASHSCORE PREVIEW

UEFA Conference League underperformers Pafos and Midtjylland clash on matchday four with both still awaiting their first win of this season’s league phase.

Match News and Current Form

Founded in 2014, Pafos’ third successive campaign in the main draw of a European competition hasn't gone to plan, collecting just one point from their opening three league phase games. For a side who reached the Conference League last 16 in 2024/25 and fought valiantly in the Champions League last term, that’s a disappointing return, although they have at least secured back-to-back domestic victories to end a six-match winless run across all competitions (D2, L4). Ricardo Sá Pinto’s side should fancy their chances at home too, having lost just one of their last nine group/league phase home matches in Europe (W6, D2), and that came against continental heavyweights Bayern Munich.

Danish Superliga table-toppers Midtjylland boast far more European experience than Pafos, but are yet to impress in their first-ever league phase appearance in this competition (D1, L2). The Wolves are hunting a response after a chastening 6-1 defeat against Ajax on matchday three which was their joint-heaviest European loss ever. That came on home turf, and hitting the road may be a blessing for Mike Tullberg’s side, who have won eight of their last 12 European away games (D2, L2) and were last beaten on their travels in any competition back in July (W8, D4).

Head-to-Head History

This is the pair’s first meeting, and Pafos’ first-ever H2H with a Danish side. Midtjylland have won only two of their eight games against Cypriot clubs (D3, L3).

Hot Stats and Streaks

Pafos’ last six European games saw both teams score.

Pafos received a joint-low two yellow cards across the first three matchdays.

Four of Midtjylland’s last eight European games have produced exactly two goals.

Midtjylland have conceded five times without reply in the second half of their league phase games this term.

Key Players to Watch and Missing Players

Ken Sema opened the scoring for Pafos at the weekend, and his other two goal involvements this term have come in Conference League home games (G1, A1). Sofus Johannesen has scored three times in Midtjylland’s last five games, while all five of his strikes this season came after half-time.

Pafos’ Lelê and Midtjylland’s Kjell Wätjen are both banned following red cards. The Danes also have a lengthy injury list including first-choice goalkeeper Nordin Bakker and Denil Castillo.

Betting Analysis

This game looks set to be pivotal for both teams' chances of reaching the knockout stages, so anticipating a slow burner, both teams to score in the second half appears viable.
