FLASHSCORE PREVIEW

Atalanta’s miserable European away form in 2026 could get worse when they visit Borac Banja Luka’s fortress in the UEFA Conference League on Thursday.

Match News and Current Form

Borac warmed up for this fixture by scoring four goals in a domestic league game for the second successive match, defeating Željezničar 4-0 away. Vinko Marinović’s men now need to bring that impressive form into the Conference League, having lost two of their opening three league-phase games (W1) this season. That solitary win came against KuPS at home, where Borac have not lost across all competitions since last December, and they could now become just the second team outside Europe's top five leagues to remain unbeaten in their first ten main-draw matches as hosts in major European competition (W6, D3).

Atalanta have not travelled well in Europe recently, losing all four such away games this calendar year excluding qualifiers - their longest streak of main-draw defeats on the road in major continental competition. Their overall form is also disappointing, having won just one of their last eight competitive matches (D4, L3), while they find themselves 16th in the Conference League ahead of this round of fixtures (W1, D1, L1). Avoiding defeat in Bosnia and Herzegovina would see La Dea go four competitive games unbeaten for only the second time since Maurizio Sarri’s appointment in June though, and they will take confidence from their 4-4 draw on Sunday against Inter Milan, achieved despite trailing by two goals on three occasions.

Head-to-Head History

Since their country gained independence, a Bosnian side have yet to beat Italian opposition (D1, L3), while Atalanta’s only previous meeting with a Bosnian team saw them thump Sarajevo 10-2 on aggregate in 2018.

Hot Stats and Streaks

Borac have received at least one first-half yellow card in all three of their league-phase games this season.

Borac kept a clean sheet or conceded only one goal in 14 of their last 15 European home matches.

The half-time result was replicated at full-time in just two of Atalanta’s last seven games.

Atalanta have had more corners than their opponents in their three league-phase matches this season.

Key Players to Watch and Missing Players

Amer Hiroš has been booked in two of Borac’s three league-phase games this term and has registered four goal contributions across their last three Bosnian top-flight matches (G2, A2). Charles De Ketelaere is also in excellent form, with five goal contributions to his name (G3, A2) in his last three games for club or country.

Branimir Cipetić, Anderson Esiti, Ante Roguljić and Stefan Savić could all miss out for Borac, while Atalanta will be without goalkeeper Marco Carnesecchi.

For all the latest team news, please check the Flashscore match centre.

Betting Analysis

Considering the two sides’ respective recent European home and away records, backing a Borac win or a draw as a double chance seems sensible here.

FLASHSCORE PREVIEW

Braga have an excellent opportunity to record a third consecutive UEFA Conference League game without defeat on Thursday when they host a KuPS side who have won only one competitive match since the start of October. 

Match News and Current Form

After winning only one competitive game from mid-September until the end of October (D1, L5), Braga have found their form in November with four clean sheets contributing to a four-game unbeaten streak (W3, D1). This recent strong defensive showing has also been a feature of their European season, where the Archbishops have registered eight shutouts from nine fixtures, although they have failed to score themselves in four of their last six. Following three consecutive away games, Braga are back at home where they have won two of their last three (L1) and Franclim Carvalho’s side should still be on a high after a 2-0 victory at local rivals Vitória de Guimarães in the Taça de Portugal on Saturday.

By the time this game begins, it will have been 18 days since KuPS last played a competitive fixture due to the completion of their domestic season, giving themselves plenty of time on the training ground to stew over their record of no wins from their last six competitive matches (D3, L3) and only two victories from their last 14 games across all competitions (D5, L7). With only two goals scored, one point on the board and just three teams below them in this competition ahead of this round, Miika Nuutinen’s side could be in for another struggle, particularly as they have not won any of their 14 away games in major European competitions (D4, L10), failing to score in ten of those clashes. 

Head-to-Head History

Braga have never previously faced a Finnish side while KuPS were beaten 1-0 on aggregate by Académica in the 1969/70 European Cup Winners’ Cup, their solitary H2H with a Portuguese team.

Hot Stats and Streaks

Braga have not conceded after half-time in any of their last seven competitive games.

None of Braga’s nine European fixtures this season, qualifiers included, saw both teams score.

KuPS have not scored a second-half goal in any of their last four competitive matches.

KuPS have picked up one booking after half-time in each of their three Conference League games this season.

Key Players to Watch and Missing Players

Ricardo Horta has not scored in Europe since the qualifiers but has five goals from his last five competitive games, opening the scoring for his team in all four scoring matches in that run. Petteri Pennanen looks like one of KuPS’ best hopes of finding the net as three of his last four competitive goal contributions have come in away fixtures (G2, A2).

Both teams appear to have no new availability issues.

For all the latest team news, please check the Flashscore match centre.

Betting Analysis

Both sides have struggled for goals in Europe so backing under 2.5 match goals is the logical approach.

FLASHSCORE PREVIEW

CSKA Sofia’s prospects of extending their UEFA Conference League campaign will dwindle further if they cannot beat a Trabzonspor outfit who still harbour top-eight ambitions.

Match News and Current Form

After a rollercoaster 3-3 draw at Botev Plovdiv at the weekend, CSKA Sofia have now lost just twice in 15 outings (W8, D5), but both of those defeats have come in this competition. Picking up just a solitary point across the first three matchdays, the Reds have managed only two victories from their last 32 major European matches (D8, L22) and sit outside the top-24 as a result. They can at least draw inspiration from being back at their newly reconstructed Stadion Balgarska Armia home, where they returned with a 0-0 draw against Slavia Sofia last month, which looks timely given that they’ve lost their last three European matches as the designated hosts.

Trabzonspor’s 1-0 victory over Eyüpspor on Sunday was a ninth win from ten matches across all competitions (L1), although that defeat came on matchday three against Freiburg (1-0). Thomas Reis’ men won their two prior league phase games to occupy a play-off place at the halfway stage, with one of those victories coming away at KuPS on matchday one. That ended a run of nine successive away defeats in major European matches, while they could now secure back-to-back wins on their continental travels for the first time since 2013.

Head-to-Head History

CSKA Sofia have lost five of their previous seven clashes with Turkish teams (W1, D1), whereas Trabzonspor are facing Bulgarian opposition for the first time.

Hot Stats and Streaks

CSKA Sofia have registered at least five shots on target in each of their three league phase games.

Each of CSKA Sofia’s three league phase matches saw both teams score and featured over 2.5 goals.

Only one of Trabzonspor’s last seven games saw both teams score.

Trabzonspor have failed to score in four of their last six European away fixtures.

Key Players to Watch and Missing Players

Five of Ioannis Pittas’ last seven goals for CSKA Sofia have served as their first or last of the game, and they’ve never lost when he’s been on target (W21, D6). Trabzonspor’s Noah Saviolo has seen both of his goals this term arrive before the 35th minute and half-time, while he’s been fouled three times in each of his last two outings in this competition.

CSKA Sofia’s Léo Pereira is out injured, while Franculino remains an injury concern for Trabzonspor.

For all the latest team news, please check the Flashscore match centre.

Betting Analysis

Despite their away day blues in this competition, Trabzonspor to win looks the sensible selection here.

FLASHSCORE PREVIEW

An intriguing UEFA Conference League clash is on the cards when one of Europe’s hottest teams right now Freiburg host a Twente side who haven’t put a foot wrong in the league phase as yet.

Match News and Current Form

After a three-game losing run in October which included a 3-0 defeat against Monaco on matchday two of this season’s league phase, Freiburg have since turned up the heat with five successive wins, with the most recent three being accompanied by clean sheets. In that run is a 1-0 win away to Trabzonspor in their last European outing before they beat Elversberg by the same score at the weekend, also away from home. Returning to the Europa-Park Stadion will only fill them further with confidence, as the Breisgau Brazilians have won their last 12 home games in major European competitions, rendering them just the second German side this century to achieve that feat.

They’ll welcome a worthy opponent in perfect starters Twente, who boast a perfect record after three league phase matches following their 3-1 win over Pafos in the last round, with this being the first time they’ve ever begun a major European campaign with three successive wins. That made it six wins from their seven major European games since the beginning of 2025 (L1), meaning their confidence will be sky high before even considering they picked up another victory when beating Willem II at the weekend and the fact they’re unbeaten in their last eight away matches (W5, D3).

Head-to-Head History

Freiburg have experienced a mixed bag of results in their three encounters with Dutch opposition (W1, D1, L1), while Twente have won just one of their nine European away games against German sides (D3, L5).

Hot Stats and Streaks

Ten of Freiburg’s last 11 European outings featured goals in both halves.

Ten of Freiburg’s 11 prior European matches featured over 2.5 goals.

Nine of Twente’s last 11 European games saw both teams score.

The half-time result was replicated at full-time in five of Twente’s last six away fixtures.

Key Players to Watch and Missing Players

Vincenzo Grifo has seen his last four goals for Freiburg come in Europe, while he’s also netted five of his last six goals at home. Twente’s Daouda Weidmann has recorded a goal involvement in all three of his UEFA Conference League games this season (G2, A2), with both goals contributing to three of his last four strikes coming after the 80th minute.

Freiburg don’t seem to be dealing with many injury concerns at the moment, while Twente were without Thomas van den Belt and Max Bruns at the weekend.

For all the latest team news, please check the Flashscore match centre.

Betting Analysis

There should be plenty of goalmouth action here and so both teams to score and over 2.5 goals seems a highly likely outcome.

FLASHSCORE PREVIEW

Gent’s wasteful attacking unit will be looking to sharpen up and increase their goal tally when they host a Red Star Belgrade side who have been scoring and conceding heavily in this UEFA Conference League campaign. 

Match News and Current Form

Gent were one of just three clubs to score only one goal across the first three matchdays of this Conference League season, with their sound defending primarily responsible for having earned four points (W1, D1, L1). Gent’s profligacy in front of goal in the competition this season stands out, with their 2% shot conversion rate (one goal from 52 shot attempts) the lowest of any side, so any improvement in their shooting accuracy could net significant returns. Their defending has also underpinned their success at home, where they have lost just one of their last 13 home games in major European competition (W9, D3), with that defeat - 3-0 against Betis in last season’s UEFA Conference League play-offs - the only time they conceded 2+ goals during that span.

Red Star Belgrade joined Gent in the middle of the table with four points, all of which were claimed at home, with only one side ahead of the round seeing more goals in their games (GF 6, GA 6) than the Serbians. Now with a dominant 11-point lead at the top of their domestic league standings, Red Star can afford to devote even more attention to their promising Conference League campaign as they attempt to advance beyond the league phase of a European competition for a second season running. The Serbian giants have now won six of their last ten major European matches (D2, L2) and, despite stumbling away to Lugano in their most recent away trip (L 3-2), can boast 1-0 wins in their three prior major European away games. 

Head-to-Head History

These teams met in the group stage of the 2020/21 Europa League with Red Star winning both contests (2-1 home and 2-0 away). 

Hot Stats and Streaks

Seven of Gent’s last nine competitive matches produced under 2.5 goals. 

Gent kept a clean sheet in seven of their last nine European wins. 

Red Star conceded a first-half goal in only one of their last nine wins in all competitions. 

Seven of Red Star’s last nine European games featured over 2.5 goals.

Key Players to Watch and Missing Players

Abdelkahar Kadri scored Gent’s only goal since their last continental outing and has won all five of his scoring appearances for the club. Osman Bukari has won his last 14 goalscoring games for any club, eight of them spread across two stints at Red Star.  

Mouhamed El Bachir Ngom and Christian Burgess headline Gent’s injuries, whilst Red Star are expected to be without Timi Elšnik, Bamba Dieng and suspended midfielder Aleksandar Katai.

For all the latest team news, please check the Flashscore match centre.

Betting Analysis

This looks like one of the most difficult games of the matchday to predict, so perhaps a draw will eventuate. 

Author: Aaron Murphy

SUMMARY
LINEUPS
FLASHSCORE PREVIEW

Hajduk Split host unbeaten St. Truiden with both sides hoping to boost their chances of automatically qualifying for the UEFA Conference League last 16.

Match News and Current Form

Hajduk Split’s promising start to the league stage took an unexpected turn when they lost 1-0 to Gibraltar’s Lincoln Red Imps on matchday three, although they remain well placed to qualify (W2, L1). The Whites beat Lokomotiva Zagreb 2-1 on Saturday to maintain a four-point lead over rivals Dinamo Zagreb atop the Croatian top-flight, and they now aim for more than two wins in one major European campaign for the first time since earning five in 1985/86. Gonzalo García’s side are also unbeaten across all 12 competitive home fixtures this term (W10, D2) - including a famous 2-1 win over Ajax - suggesting they’ll take some beating here despite this game being played behind closed doors due to UEFA sanctions against Hajduk.

St. Truiden are one point better off than their hosts (W2, D1), conceding just one goal during an impressive maiden major European campaign. Struggling to match that defensive resilience elsewhere cost Frédéric De Meyer his job earlier this month, with Jonas De Roeck back for a second spell as head coach as the Canaries sit an underwhelming 11th in the Belgian Pro League. They’ve conceded an average of two goals per domestic league game this season, but could instead take heart from winning away at Midtjylland on matchday two (1-0) and drawing 2-2 at Charleroi on Saturday in their most recent trip.

Head-to-Head History

This will be the first-ever H2H. Hajduk have won five of their six home European games against Belgian opposition (L1), while St. Truiden have never previously faced Croatian opponents.

Hot Stats and Streaks

Only Thun (68) committed more fouls across the first three matchdays than Hajduk (59).

Four of Hajduk’s five home European games this term produced at least two second-half goals.

Four of St. Truiden’s five European games this term saw at least one goal after the 75th minute.

St. Truiden conceded 2+ goals in four of their last five away fixtures.

Key Players to Watch and Missing Players

Michele Šego has six goal contributions (G5, A1) across Hajduk’s Conference League campaign this season and has opened the scoring in six of his nine goalscoring appearances this term. Ilias Sebaoui has netted in both of St. Truiden’s last two fixtures, with three of his last four goals arriving after the 50th minute.

Abdoulie Sanyang and Marin Šotiček missed Hajduk’s weekend win but may feature here, while St. Truiden do not appear to have any major injury worries.

For all the latest team news, please check the Flashscore match centre.

Betting Analysis

Hajduk’s superb home record in all competitions this term could be too much for a St. Truiden side under new management, so backing Hajduk to win holds appeal.

Author: John Pennington

FLASHSCORE PREVIEW

Inter Escaldes look to avoid defeat in a major European game for the first time against UEFA Conference League high-flyers Copenhagen, who travel after a galling domestic defeat.

Match News and Current Form

Inter Escaldes may be unbeaten domestically in Andorra so far this season, but their first-ever UEFA main draw appearance has proven a huge challenge. They’re one of just two sides to suffer defeat on each of the opening three matchdays, though they came agonisingly close to posting their first point last time out when they gave up the lead and conceded decisively beyond the 90th minute to lose 2-1 against Red Star Belgrade. If Inter are to finally enjoy success at this level, it’s likely to happen at home where they’ve been beaten just once since March (W9, D2), and though that reversal came in the league phase, it accounts for half of their defeats across their last 11 European home games (W5, D4, L2). 

Copenhagen’s eight-match unbeaten run (W5, D3) was unceremoniously ended on Sunday as they were thrashed 5-0 by Nordsjælland. Manager Bo Svensson will hope that was just a temporary blip given that the Lions have made their best-ever start to a European group/league phase (W2, D1), although they were far from convincing in a 2-1 win over Georgian minnows Iberia on matchday three. While the calibre of their opposition here gives reason for confidence, Copenhagen are also far from bulletproof on the road where they’ve secured just one win in their last five European trips (D3, L1).

Head-to-Head History

These sides have never met previously, though Danish teams have won all six previous meetings with Andorran opponents in Europe, scoring 17 goals while conceding just one.

Hot Stats and Streaks

Just three sides attempted fewer shots than Inter (22) across the first three matchdays.

Just three of Inter’s last nine home games saw both teams score.

Copenhagen have scored four unanswered goals after half-time in the league phase.

Only two sides committed fewer fouls than Copenhagen (28) pre-matchday.

Key Players to Watch and Missing Players

Borja Arellano has scored both of Inter’s goals in the league phase and has netted in a 1-1 domestic draw since, meaning none of his last three scoring appearances ended in victory (D1, L2). Mohamed Elyounoussi has scored or assisted in four of his last six major European appearances (G3, A1), and has seen 14 of his 21 direct goal involvements in Europe come in away matches. 

Inter are without the suspended Domi Berlanga, while Copenhagen expect to be without goalkeeper Diant Ramaj after he picked up an injury at the weekend.

For all the latest team news, please check the Flashscore match centre.

Betting Analysis

This ought to be one of the most one-sided games in this competition, so backing a Copenhagen victory by 2+ goals certainly makes sense.

Author: Ryan Fisher

FLASHSCORE PREVIEW

Nordsjælland put a strong European home record on the line when they host Panathinaikos, who have a burgeoning reputation on the continental scene. 

Match News and Current Form

Nordsjælland pulled off a shock result in the Danish Superliga on Sunday as they downed league leaders Copenhagen 5-0 at home. That brought a timely end to a winless three-match home run prior for the Danish side, who have tended to do their best work in Europe on home turf, where they’re unbeaten in four matches in major European competition. A failure to keep a clean sheet in the last nine major European matches they hosted should be enough to keep feet firmly on the ground though, as they seek their first win of this league phase cycle (D2, L1). 

Panathinaikos have arguably exceeded expectations in this Conference League this term, posting nine points from their opening three matches (W3), with all three wins bedded within a nine-game winning run in competitive action. In a four-way share of the Conference League lead pre-round and with their spot in the knockouts almost certainly assured, the Greek Super League leaders replicating their run to the last 16 of this competition in 2024/25 is looking increasingly likely. Panathinaikos have been quietly improving on the European scene for quite some time now, considering they’ve lost just one of their last 12 matches in major European competition (W6, D5), as they look to open a continental campaign with four successive victories for the first time since 2007/08. 

Head-to-Head History

Nordsjælland have lost their last four games against Greek opposition, while Panathinaikos have lost three of their five major European matches against teams from Denmark (W2).

Hot Stats and Streaks

Nordsjælland picked up the most yellow cards in the first three league phase rounds (11). 

Nordsjælland scored 2+ goals in five of their last six home games.

Only one side took more corners than Panathinaikos (27) across the opening three rounds.

Panathinaikos’ nine games in European competition (including qualifiers) this season all saw both teams score. 

Key Players to Watch and Missing Players

Nordsjælland’s Alexander Lind is in sensational form at present, contributing to eight goals in his last two appearances (G4, A4), with three of those goals arriving after the 70th minute. Elmin Rastoder could grow into the game for Panathinaikos having netted his last five goals for club or country in the second half. 

Tobias Salquist was missing in Nordsjælland’s last game, while Panathinaikos’ Santino Andino picked up an injury in their weekend outing.

For all the latest team news, please check the Flashscore match centre.

Betting Analysis

Considering the form Panathinaikos are in on the European circuit, an away win is priced up rather attractively. 

Author: Chris Wilson
